headline: Learned models rank enzymes, reactions, kinetics and mutants, now tested against stricter benchmarks and wet-lab data
label: Learned Enzyme Candidate Prioritization
summary: New work pairs learned enzyme prioritization with reaction-disjoint benchmarks, campaign-grouped kinetic data and experimental screening, including a 150-mutant validation.
synthesis: The shared thread is learned ranking or selection of enzyme-related candidates: enzyme-reaction pairs (RIVER), kcat and Km (KineCouple), active enzymes versus decoys and EC numbers (DecoyOpt), fungal peroxygenase substrates, and mutants (EnzyArena). Some methods build on pretrained encoders, such as frozen ProtT5/MolT5 in KineCouple and ESM3-generated decoys in DecoyOpt. The newer emphasis is on evaluation and validation. EnzyArena groups kinetic data by campaign, compares 20 models, finds zero-shot consensus best, and validates with 150 mutants. The generative-reaction study uses a reaction-disjoint benchmark to test reactions absent from training. The peroxygenase workflow combines sequence mining, expression-aware prioritization, wet-lab screening and gradient-boosting models. Tasks and scope differ, so this is a common direction rather than a single method.
